items.text: In overweight dogs with osteoarthritis seen in 12 first-opinion practices, does a nurse-led weight clinic, compared with usual vet-led advice, improve owner-reported mobility on the 11-item index at six months?
items.population: Overweight dogs (body condition score 7 or more of 9) with osteoarthritis diagnosed by a vet, seen in the group's 12 practices
items.intervention: Nurse-led weight clinic: monthly weigh-ins, measured food allowance with therapeutic diet, exercise plan and phone check-in
items.comparator: Usual vet-led advice with a diet leaflet, same discounted diet available
items.outcome: Change in owner-reported mobility and comfort index (0 to 44) from baseline to six months

finer: Feasible with the group's nurses and about 45 eligible dogs a month; interesting to owners and the board; novel in first-opinion practice; ethical with written consent and welfare monitoring; relevant to the roll-out decision.
summary: One PICOT question for the primary comparison.
